- Overestimate prices in the short term after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (e.g., +0.17 or higher) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.28 or lower) — model fails to account for downward pressure, leading to lagged corrections.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overreacts to recent highs, causing overforecasting in the next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds too much upward bias after peaks, even when sentiment turns negative.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive, then underestimates later (last 5–7 days) when sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days, model should reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for potential reversal.
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, model should not extrapolate beyond 2–3 days — avoid long-term bullish bias unless sentiment is sustained.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model should average recent 3–5 day trends rather than following 18-day history.
